newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: JNOC signs $50.5 million Kazakh offshore oil deal.
newsitem.headline: JNOC signs $50.5 million Kazakh offshore oil deal.

text.p: The Japan National Oil Corporation (JNOC) signed a deal on Monday to spend over $50 million prospecting for oil offshore Kazakhstan, company and government officials said.
JNOC President Kunio Komatsu told a news conference in Almaty that the company eventually hoped to produce oil from Kazakhstan's resource-rich Caspian Sea shelf.
"Japan would like to be alloted part of the Caspian Sea shelf for oil extraction and is ready to take part in an oil exploration tender once it has been announced," he said.
He declined to give further details.
A Kazakh government statement said that under the deal signed on Monday, JNOC would explore oil reserves in Kazakh sections of the Aral Sea and Caspian Sea.
It said JNOC would invest $50.5 million over an unspecified period of time, including $40 million for exploration and test drilling in the Aral Sea.

Kazakhstan said in June that a seismic survey of its Caspian Sea continental shelf had shown huge, estimated crude oil reserves of 10 billion tonnes and natural gas reserves of two trillion cubic metres.
